_comment: Guided tour for particle tracking in the emtk window. Targets are the spec's attr names and the headers and buttons the window draws; steps that need the user to act wait (await) and never press anything. The help page carries the long form.

steps.title: Three stages, and each can be wrong on its own
steps.text: Detect where the particles are in each frame, link them into trajectories, then read transport (D and the anomalous exponent) from the mean squared displacement. They fail independently and quietly: a bad detector gives short tracks, a bad linker gives long wrong ones, a bad MSD fit gives a reasonable-looking D.

steps.title: Start with a movie whose answer you know
steps.text: Load example writes a movie of six particles diffusing with D = 0.5 px²/frame and tracks them, so the diffusion coefficient the tool reports can be checked against the truth.

steps.title: Start with a movie whose answer you know
steps.text: Another way to a known answer: the Simulate instead panel generates Brownian particles with a diffusion coefficient you choose, so the result can be checked against a number. Any TIFF stack or photon stream works the same way once dropped on the ChiSurf window and picked in the Input section.

steps.title: Switch to the simulation
steps.text: With Simulate ticked the tool ignores the file field and tracks a generated movie. The true D below is what the fit should give back.

steps.title: Detection: count them before you believe them
steps.text: The report states the detections per frame: compare it with what you expect. Too many means you are tracking noise and the extras steal links; too few means the dim particles are missing. Min area and Min separation decide this.

steps.title: Max step is the entire safety margin
steps.text: Linking is a global assignment, not nearest neighbour. Set Max step from the physics, about sqrt(4 D dt) per frame, never from what makes the tracks look longest: too large joins different particles, too small shatters every trajectory.

steps.title: Track
steps.text: Detection, linking and the MSD fit run in the background; the status line counts the frames.

await.hint: Press Track and wait for the status line to give D.

steps.title: Check the movie
steps.text: Scrub the Z slice slider or press Play: markers that follow the particles mean detection works, markers that flicker mean the threshold is too high, markers on empty background mean it is too low.

steps.title: Read the MSD
steps.text: On log axes free diffusion is a straight line of slope 1. The model is MSD = 4 D t^alpha + 4 sigma^2: the offset is the localisation error and must not be dropped, and only short lags are fitted.

steps.title: Fit alpha only when that is the question
steps.text: alpha near 1 is normal diffusion, below 1 subdiffusive, above 1 directed. D and alpha are nearly degenerate: fitting both roughly quadruples the spread of D, and merged tracks from crowding fake directed motion. The Help button has the rest.
